'''Dale Vance Holliday''' (May 29, 1940 &ndash; February 4, 2010) was an American physicist and acoustician.

Born in [[Ennis, Texas]], Holliday attended the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] and [[Master's degree|M.A.]] in [[Physics]] and did extensive [[theoretical]] and [[experiment]]al research on the [[Mössbauer effect]]. He died in [[San Diego]] on February 4, 2010, after a period of illness.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/signonsandiego/obituary.aspx?n=dale-vance-holliday&pid=140004089 |title=DALE HOLLIDAY Obituary |work=San Diego Union Tribune |accessdate=2010-03-06}}</ref>

Holliday became one of the first 100 employees of [[Tracor]] in 1962 and quickly became Director of Analysis and Applied Research in the Electronic Systems Division. In 1965 Holliday left Austin to develop the Tracor facility in [[San Diego, California|San Diego]] and began his [[doctorate]] in [[applied physics]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]].

In [[San Diego, California|San Diego]] Holliday began his study in [[acoustics]] for which he is known. His study of transient flow in [[natural gas]] [[pipeline transport|pipelines]] led to the publication of a [[textbook]] which is still used as a standard reference.

In the 1970s Holliday began testing a revolutionary technique for the detection and size measurement of zooplankton in [[thin layers (oceanography)|thin layers]] involving multi-frequency backscattering. The technique developed and after twenty years became the established framework for research in the field.

In the early 1980s Holliday built the first prototype of the Tracor Acoustical Profiling System (TAPS) which has been described as decades ahead of its time by the Acoustical Society of America. TAPS is now the standard instrument for acoustical profiling of [[plankton]] in the sea.{{Citation needed|date=February 2010}}

Holliday published hundreds of papers on [[underwater acoustics]] and [[acoustical oceanography]] and given dozens of talks and symposia in several countries. In 2004 Holliday became only the third recipient of the [[Acoustical Society of America]] [[ASA Silver Medal|Silver Medal]] in Acoustical Oceanography, for "contributions to the study of [[marine life]], from plankton to [[whales]]".<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2005-09-01|title=Acoustical News—USA|journal=The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America|volume=118|issue=3|pages=1223–1242|doi=10.1121/1.1999958|issn=0001-4966|doi-access=free|bibcode=2005ASAJ..118.1223. }}</ref>

Holliday was awarded the Prix d'Excellence by the [[International Council for the Exploration of the Sea]] (ICES) in recognition of extraordinary contributions, fulfilling the ICES vision of scientific discovery, leadership, and applications that have had major influence on policy for sustained use and conservation of marine ecosystems. The Award was presented at the ICES Annual Science Conference on Monday September 22, 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ices.dk/iceswork/asc/2008/NEWS/mondayASC.asp |title=ASC News 2008 |publisher=Ices.dk |year=2008 |accessdate=2010-02-05 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101207024519/http://www.ices.dk/iceswork/asc/2008/NEWS/mondayASC.asp |archivedate=2010-12-07 }}</ref>

The research vessel R/V Dale Van Holliday is operated by the [[Southwest Fisheries Science Center]] of the [[NOAA]] Fisheries Service.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://swfsc.noaa.gov/textblock.aspx?Division=FRD&ParentMenuId=294&id=2292 |title=Instrumented Small Craft - SWFSC |publisher=Swfsc.noaa.gov |date=23 December 2005 |accessdate=2010-02-05}}</ref>

Holliday died on February 4, 2010, at the age of 69 from complications of heart surgery, which was in turn caused by complications from the [[scoliosis]] which he had battled his entire life.

The Acoustical Society of America organized a [http://scitation.aip.org/journals/doc/ASALIB-home/corp/pdf/meetings/sdcalendar.pdf session in his memory] during its 162nd Meeting, on October 31, 2011.

==Honors and Positions==
* Prix d'Excellence - [[International Council for the Exploration of the Sea]] (2008)
* [[ASA Silver Medal|Silver Medal]] in [[acoustical oceanography]] - [[Acoustical Society of America]] (2004)
* Meritorious Public Service Award - Department of the Navy, Chief of Naval Research (2002)
* Founding Editorial Board - [[American Society of Limnology and Oceanography|Limnology and Oceanography: Methods]] (2002)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aslo.org/lomethods/information/masthead.html |title=ASLO Masthead |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100601050858/http://www.aslo.org/lomethods/information/masthead.html |archivedate=2010-06-01 }}</ref>
* Steinbach Visiting Scholar - [[Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution]] (1987)
* Member of the US Delegation to the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (1987)
* R/V D. V. Holliday - [[NOAA]]
